target: C'est un pays dont la culture est fascinante.
english: It's a country whose culture is fascinating.
tip: Dont means "whose" here, and French keeps the article: dont la culture = "whose culture." You never drop the la the way English drops "the."

target: C'est la collègue dont le mari est pilote.
english: She's the colleague whose husband is a pilot.
tip: French drops "a" before a job after être: est pilote = "is a pilot," not "est un pilote." The article returns only once you describe the job.

target: Les informations que vous m'avez données sont très utiles.
english: The information you gave me is very useful.
tip: Information is plural in French: les informations... sont takes a plural verb, while English keeps "information is" singular and uncountable.

target: L'entreprise dont il est le directeur est en pleine croissance.
english: The company he is the director of is growing rapidly.
tip: "Dont" replaces "de" in all constructions: être directeur de → dont.

target: Je craignais qu'elle ne mourût de froid.
english: I feared she might die of cold.
tip: That 'ne' after 'craindre' isn't a negation: 'qu'elle ne mourût' means fearing she WOULD die, not that she wouldn't.

target: Or, personne n'avait prévu cette situation.
english: Now, no one had foreseen this situation.
tip: Or: 'now/however', introduces a new and often contradictory fact.

target: Il fallait que chacun fît sa part.
english: Everyone had to do their part.
tip: 'fît' is bookish – the literary past subjunctive. Spoken French reaches for the present instead: 'il fallait que chacun fasse sa part'.

target: Dès que le colis sera arrivé, je vous enverrai un courriel.
english: As soon as the package has arrived, I'll send you an email.
tip: English says 'as soon as it has arrived', but French demands the future after 'dès que': 'dès que le colis sera arrivé'.

target: Nous leur avons laissé un message.
english: We left them a message.
tip: 'Leur' here means 'to them', not just 'them': 'nous leur avons laissé' = we left a message TO them. It's the give-to pronoun, distinct from 'les' (them as direct object).

target: Je souhaitais qu'elle vînt me voir.
english: I wished she would come see me.
tip: 'Vînt' looks like a typo but it's the imperfect subjunctive, a literary tense. In everyday speech you'd just say 'qu'elle vienne me voir'.

target: Il semblait qu'il eût oublié sa promesse.
english: It seemed he had forgotten his promise.
tip: Pluperfect subjunctive: eût oublié. Literary equivalent of 'ait oublié'.

target: Quand bien même il aurait raison, je refuserais.
english: Even if he were right, I would refuse.
tip: 'quand bien même' = 'even if', but unlike 'si' it takes the conditional: 'quand bien même il aurait raison' = even if he were right.

target: On a beau chercher, on ne trouve pas la solution.
english: No matter how hard we look, we can't find the solution.
tip: Avoir beau + verb has nothing to do with beauty: 'on a beau chercher' means 'no matter how hard we search'. It sets up wasted effort, then the letdown.

target: Quoique la nuit fût sombre, il avançait.
english: Although the night was dark, he pressed on.
tip: One word or two flips the meaning: 'quoique' (one word, as here) = 'although'; 'quoi que' (two words) = 'whatever'. Quoique la nuit fût sombre = although the night was dark.

target: C'était le seul homme qui eût du courage.
english: He was the only man who had courage.
tip: After 'le seul ... qui', French switches to the subjunctive: 'le seul homme qui eût du courage'. The claim reads as a judgement, not plain fact.

target: Bien qu'il fît nuit, ils continuèrent leur route.
english: Although it was dark, they continued on their way.
tip: French uses faire for the state of the sky: 'il fait nuit' means 'it's dark', literally 'it makes night'. That's why the verb here shows up as 'fît'.

target: Avant que le soleil ne se couchât, ils partirent.
english: Before the sun set, they departed.
tip: The 'ne' in 'avant que le soleil ne se couchât' isn't a negation – it's a decorative 'ne' that 'avant que' attracts. The sun still sets.

target: Même si tu me suppliais, je ne changerais pas d'avis.
english: Even if you begged me, I wouldn't change my mind.
tip: 'même si' = 'even if', yet it takes the plain imperfect, never the subjunctive: 'même si tu me suppliais'. (Contrast 'bien que', which does.)

target: À condition que chacun y mette du sien, le projet aboutira.
english: Provided everyone does their part, the project will succeed.
tip: 'Mettre du sien' means to pull your weight, literally 'to put some of one's own'. 'Chacun y mette du sien' = everyone pitches in.

target: On dirait qu'il va pleuvoir.
english: It looks like it's going to rain.
tip: "On dirait" is literally "one would say," but it means "it looks like." On dirait qu'il va pleuvoir = the sky looks like rain – nobody is actually speaking.

target: Elle a voulu savoir où j'habitais.
english: She wanted to know where I lived.
tip: Tucked inside a sentence, a question keeps normal word order – no inversion: 'où j'habitais', not 'où habitais-je': 'elle a voulu savoir où j'habitais'.

target: Il se peut qu'elle ait changé d'avis.
english: It's possible she changed her mind.
tip: French changes an opinion, not a mind: "changer d'avis" is literally "change of opinion," with no possessive word. Elle a changé d'avis = she changed her mind.

target: Si j'étais toi, je n'accepterais pas cette offre.
english: If I were you, I wouldn't accept that offer.
tip: 'Si j'étais toi' – imparfait after 'si' for present hypotheticals. Never conditional after 'si'.

target: Le professeur a fait travailler les élèves toute la matinée.
english: The teacher made the students work all morning.
tip: 'faire' + infinitive = make someone do something, and the doer follows the pair: 'a fait travailler les élèves' – literally 'made work the students'.

target: Quand bien même cela serait possible, je n'en ai pas envie.
english: Even if that were possible, I don't feel like it.
tip: "Quand bien même" means "even if," but it takes the conditional, not the subjunctive you might expect here: quand bien même cela serait possible (serait = would be).

target: Je veux un livre qui soit intéressant et facile à lire.
english: I want a book that is interesting and easy to read.
tip: French switches to the subjunctive when the thing you want may not exist yet: "un livre qui soit intéressant" uses soit, not est – any such book, not one specific one.

target: Pour peu qu'il fasse un effort, il réussira.
english: If he makes even the slightest effort, he'll succeed.
tip: 'Pour peu que' + subjunctive: 'for little that' = if only slightly. Triggers subjunctive.

target: À moins que vous n'ayez une meilleure idée, procédons ainsi.
english: Unless you have a better idea, let's proceed this way.
tip: The n' in "vous n'ayez" is not a negative – it's a bare ne that French tacks on after à moins que. The sentence means unless you have an idea, not unless you don't.

target: Il vous suffit de signer en bas de la page.
english: You simply need to sign at the bottom of the page.
tip: "Il vous suffit de" is impersonal – literally "it suffices to you" = all you have to do is. Il vous suffit de signer = you just need to sign, nothing more.

target: Ces tableaux ont été peints par un artiste local.
english: These paintings were painted by a local artist.
tip: In the passive the participle quietly agrees: 'peints' takes -s to match 'ces tableaux' – a match English has no way to show.
